claims: The International Space Station (ISS) is a habitable artificial satellite in low Earth orbit.
The ISS serves as a microgravity research laboratory for NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), and CSA (Canada).
The ISS operates at ~408 km altitude.
The ISS has been continuously inhabited since 2000.
As of early April 2026, the ISS is transitioning crew.
Expedition 74 members recently engaged in joint operations with Artemis II.
The ISS orbits roughly every 90 minutes.
The ISS's total costs are estimated to exceed $100 billion over its lifespan.
The ISS's costs are shared by international partners.
The ISS has over 916 cubic meters of pressurized space.
The ISS is expected to continue operations until 2030.
The ISS is planned to be deorbited after 2030.
